![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/2b7a0fe3a80bfa6a0e0d82ab46a94740ce4b73007ae9d17ceb83170bce4559ff.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. The $x$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{1}{6}.$ Rounded to two decimal places, what is the measure of the angle $\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14222207/assets/eaf0e0a6434b454b58a8f53de0445bff8bae14d8bd1ec9e8e9598f0bd80323d9.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $x=\frac{1}{6}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta =\frac{1}{6}.
$$

We compute the angle $\theta $ using the inverse cosine:

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{6})=(80.405\,93…)^{∘}≈{80.41}^{∘}
$$
